How to sew a bag bottom: boxed corners and 3 more ways

How to give a bag a bottom it can stand on, four ways: the tote's folded-in bottom (two folds stitched 6 cm from the centre, so the corners form by themselves), cut-out corners, boxed corners and a separate bottom panel. Each one is animated, with advice on when to choose it.

Ways to make it

Folded-in bottom

Two stitched folds, tucked in before the side seams: the corners form by themselves.

When to choose it

When the bag is cut in one piece, folded across the middle, and you want a flat bottom with no corner seams: the corners form by themselves when the bag is turned out.

Overview

The folded-in bottom

The tote's bottom, the bag upside down: a flat 12 cm (4¾ in) base between two stitched folds, and corners that form by themselves — no corner seams. Tap the bag to stand it up.

  1. 1Base — flat, 12 cm (4¾ in) wide: the bottom between the two stitched folds
  2. 2Stitched folds — a fold stitched close to the edge, 6 cm (2⅜ in) each side of the centre crease · the long edges of the base
  3. 3Centre crease — the middle of the bottom · tucked 6 cm (2⅜ in) inside before the side seams are sewn
  4. 4Side seams — 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in), sewn with the bottom tucked in · four layers at the bottom
  5. 5Corners — formed by themselves where the side seams caught the tucked bottom · no corner seams

Step-by-step instructions

  1. The bag is cut in one piece, folded across the middle: the bottom is in the middle of the piece.

    Fold it in half across the middle and press a crease with the iron. Open it out again: the crease is the middle of the bottom.

    Measure 6 cm (2⅜ in) from the crease towards each end and draw a line across the whole width of the piece with an air-erasable pen.

  2. Fold the piece along the first line, right sides together, and stitch close to the fold, all the way across. Open it out.

    Fold and stitch along the second line the same way.

    The two stitched folds, 12 cm (4¾ in) apart, are the edges of the bottom; the centre crease is its middle. In the next step the piece bends at these folds.

    Machine: straight stitch

  3. Lay the piece right side up and lift both ends, so it bends at the two stitched folds.

    Bring the ends together. The 12 cm (4¾ in) bottom folds in on itself and the centre crease goes inside, 6 cm (2⅜ in) up between the layers — like the bottom of a paper bag.

    Lay it flat, right sides together. The stitched folds are now the bottom edge.

  4. Clip the sides so the tucked-in bottom stays in place.

    Sew both side seams, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, all the way down. At the bottom the seam goes through four layers — the front, the two halves of the tucked bottom and the back. Leave the top open.

    On the tote, the lining is sewn the same way — only one of its side seams is left with an opening, to turn the bag through later.

    Machine: straight stitch

  5. Turn the bag right side out through the top.

    Open it up and push the bottom out. The tucked bottom unfolds into a flat 12 cm (4¾ in) base, and where the side seams caught it, neat corners form by themselves — no extra corner seams needed.

Cut-out corners

A small piece cut from each bottom corner, then the corner opened and sewn straight across.

When to choose it

When the bag is folded at the bottom, its sides are sewn first and you want a flat bottom: with the corners cut out, the seams meet neatly, and it suits thicker fabrics too.

Overview

Cut-out corners

The makeup bag's bottom, the bag upside down: a flat bottom with a short seam straight across each end, where the side seam meets the bottom fold. Tap the bag to stand it up.

In this step
  • Janome HD2200 Heavy-Duty Sewing Machine (paid link)
  1. 1Bottom — flat · between the two corner seams
  2. 2Bottom fold — the 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in) piece folded in half · no seam on the bottom
  3. 3Corner seams — sewn straight across, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, after a 3.5 × 2.5 cm (1⅜ × 1 in) piece was cut from the corner
  4. 4Side seams — 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) · each meets the middle of a corner seam

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Lay the 23 × 31 cm (9 × 12¼ in) piece right side up.

    Fold it in half across its length, right sides together. The fold is the bottom of the bag — there is no seam there.

    The makeup bag's lining is the same 23 × 31 cm piece and is made the same way.

  2. Clip the sides together.

    Sew both side seams, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, all the way down to the fold.

    On the makeup bag the zipper is sewn in first, and one side seam of the lining keeps an opening for turning; the corners are made the same way.

    Machine: straight stitch

  3. Mark a 3.5 × 2.5 cm (1⅜ × 1 in) rectangle in each bottom corner: 3.5 cm along the bottom fold, 2.5 cm up the side seam.

    Cut it out through both layers.

    On the makeup bag that is four corners: two on the outer, two on the lining.

  4. Open the cut corner, pulling the front and the back apart.

    Flatten it so that the side seam lies right on the bottom fold.

    The cut edges now form one straight line across the corner.

  5. Sew straight across the corner, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

    Do the other corner the same way — on the makeup bag, the two corners of the lining too.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Turn the bag right side out (the makeup bag turns through the opening in its lining) and push the corners out.

    The bottom is flat. At each end the side seam meets the middle of the corner seam.

Boxed corners (pinched)

The bag is sewn first, then each bottom corner is flattened into a triangle and sewn straight across.

When to choose it

When you want to try the depth first: nothing is cut beforehand, so you can still sew a deeper bottom. The corner is strong, and it suits light fabrics.

Overview

Boxed corners (pinched)

The bag's bottom, the bag upside down: a flat bottom with the bottom seam along its middle and a short seam straight across each end, where the side seam meets it. Tap the bag to stand it up.

  1. 1Bottom — flat · as wide as the corner seams are long
  2. 2Bottom seam — joins the front and the back · along the middle of the bottom
  3. 3Corner seams — sewn straight across the corner, half the base width from the end of the seam
  4. 4Side seams — each meets the middle of a corner seam

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Lay the front on the back, right sides together, and clip them.

    Sew both sides and the bottom.

    Nothing is cut from the corners: the bottom is made in the next steps.

    If the bag is one piece folded at the bottom, there is no bottom seam: the side seam then goes onto the bottom fold.

    Machine: straight stitch

  2. Pull the front and the back apart at one bottom corner.

    Flatten the corner so that the side seam lies exactly on the bottom seam (or on the bottom fold).

    The corner is now a triangle, with the seam running down its middle to the end of the seam at its point.

    Open the other bottom corner the same way.

    In the drawing the bag stands on its open top, bottom up, so both corners are in view.

  3. Decide how wide the bottom should be: that is the base width.

    Measure half the base width along the seam, from the end of the seam, where the stitching meets at the point — not from the tip of the fabric.

    Draw a line there straight across the triangle, at right angles to the seam. It is as long as the base is wide.

    The farther the line is from the point, the wider the base. Mark the other corner the same way.

  4. Sew along the line, from one edge of the triangle to the other.

    Backstitch at the start and at the end, so the seam holds.

    Sew the other corner the same way.

    Machine: straight stitch

  5. Cut off the tip along the stitching, leaving a small seam allowance.

    Do not cut into the stitching.

    Make every bottom corner the same way, and the lining's corners too if the bag has a lining.

  6. Turn the bag right side out and push the corners out.

    The bottom is flat and as wide as the line across was long. At each end the side seam meets the middle of the corner seam.

Separate bottom panel

The base is a piece of its own, sewn into the bottom of the walls all round.

When to choose it

When you want a flat, stable base, a base in another fabric, or a firm one with interfacing or an insert. Round and oval bases are sewn in too, with the walls' allowance snipped into all along the curve.

Overview

Separate bottom panel

The bag's bottom, the bag upside down: the base is a piece of its own, here in another fabric, sewn to the walls all round. Tap the bag to stand it up.

  1. 1Base — a separate piece · here in another fabric
  2. 2Base seam — joins the walls to the base, all round
  3. 3Corners — the walls' seam allowance snipped into, so the corner stays sharp
  4. 4Side seams — each meets the middle of a short side of the base

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Lay the front on the back, right sides together, and fasten them with sewing clips.

    Sew both sides, from top to bottom.

    The tube stays open at the bottom too: the base is a separate piece, sewn in later.

    If the walls are cut in one piece, a single seam closes the tube.

    Machine: straight stitch

  2. Fold the base in half and crease the fold with the iron or your fingers.

    Unfold it, fold it in half the other way and crease again.

    Make a mark at the middle of each side, at the edge, where a crease meets it.

    Fold the tube in half, side seam on side seam, and crease it: the creases mark the middle of the front and of the back.

    The side seams are marks too: the tube is marked in quarters, like the base.

  3. The tube is wrong side out and the base lies right side up, so the right sides face each other.

    Line up the edges of the tube and the base all round; the walls' seam allowance lies on the edge of the base.

    First match the marks: each side seam on the middle of a short side, each crease on the middle of a long side.

    Fasten the marks with sewing clips first, then add more clips in between.

  4. Find where each corner of the base meets the walls.

    With the scissors, snip the walls' seam allowance into the corner, to just short of the seam line: not through the stitching.

    The allowance then opens and lies flat round the corner, and the corner stays sharp.

    Snip all the corners the same way.

  5. Sew with the tube wrong side out, on the seam line.

    Start in the middle of a side, with a backstitch.

    Stop one seam allowance from the corner, with the needle down in the fabric.

    Lift the presser foot, turn the corner, lower the foot and sew the next side.

    Take out the clips as you come to them and sew all the way round; backstitch where you started.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Turn the bag right side out and push out the corners.

    The base lies flat, and the seam runs round its edge.

    For a firm base, the stiffening goes on the base: interfacing ironed on before it is sewn in, or a firm insert laid in afterwards.
